definitions: One should not make judgments about the worth or value of something or someone based solely on outward appearance.
Appearances can be misleading; true nature or quality is not always evident from the surface.
examples: The old house looked rundown, but inside it was beautifully renovated; you can't judge a book by its cover.
He seemed quiet and shy at first, but he's actually very outgoing once you get to know him. You really can't judge a book by its cover.
Don't dismiss that restaurant just because of its plain exterior; you can't judge a book by its cover, and their food is amazing.
lemma: you can't judge a book by its cover
source: you can't judge a book by its cover
